doc.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20

title: Navy marches versus New Orleans marches, wrap-up
summary: Gorman describes the marches played in the Navy versus New Orleans, as Allen closes for the sleeve notes.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Oh, I see. Let's see, what other things can I ask you about? I think we just about got enough for a little write-up on the sleeve, so we can catch it now. Do you want to tell me something?
Well, you might want to ask me when I was in the Navy, what type of music I was playing. What did you play? Well, that's what you want to ask me.
Well, alright then. When I was in the Navy, we used to play marches, such as Suzie's March, Thunder, Light Cab, no, I mean Thunder, Stars and Stripes, Glory, Chicago Tribune, all those kinds.
Did they play those in New Orleans? Sure. They play them in New Orleans?
They do play that in the Navy. But not in New Orleans.
What kind of numbers would they play in New Orleans?

Well, we would play marches, but there wasn't heavy marches that night. See, there wasn't heavy marches that night. You know what I mean? They'd play like marches, like say, well, especially when you march, any number you play, if you drill in, it's a march, you see. Well, you played it when the saints come march, you know, and all. Well, I mean, all the different numbers.
Well, what about the written numbers in New Orleans, not the head numbers in the brass band?
